title: Defend the Roadmap
subtitle: Your quarterly product roadmap vs. a skeptical exec
description: You are the Product Manager presenting Q3 roadmap to the SVP of Sales who thinks you are prioritising the wrong features. Defend your decisions under pressure.
learning_objectives: Defend a data-informed position against authority pressure
Recognise common executive pushback patterns: sunk-cost, customer anecdote, urgency manipulation
Learn to disagree professionally without being dismissive
reflection_prompt: At what point in the debate did you feel most under pressure, and how did you handle it?
coaching_moment: Defending a roadmap is not the same as being inflexible. The strongest PMs distinguish between data-backed changes and capitulation under social pressure.

scoring_anchors_summary.win: Held the roadmap with evidence, acknowledged the exec's customer signal, offered a structured fast-follow, and named at least one pressure tactic.
scoring_anchors_summary.draw: Stood firm on most items but made an unwarranted concession under authority pressure without data.
scoring_anchors_summary.lose: Rewrote the roadmap based on anecdote. Shipped the wrong features. Missed the quarter's real objective.

ai_opponent.name: SVP Ramesh
ai_opponent.opening_argument: I just came from three customer calls. Every single one of them asked for the bulk-export feature you cut from Q3. You need to add it back.

scenarios.title: Defend the Q3 Roadmap
scenarios.description: Defend your data-driven product roadmap against a senior stakeholder who wants to reprioritise based on anecdotal customer feedback.

ai_persona.name: SVP Ramesh
ai_persona.style: Opens with customer anecdotes, escalates with urgency, uses authority as final lever.

scenarios.coaching_tips: Name the tactic before you counter it. 'That is a valuable customer signal — and here is how it ranks against the 200 data points in the research.' Avoid saying 'no' directly. Instead: 'Not in Q3 — here is why, and here is when.'
learning_objectives: Defend data-informed prioritisation under authority pressure
Propose structured alternatives rather than flat refusals

storybook_pages.title: You Built the Plan
storybook_pages.text: Six weeks of research. Forty customer interviews. OKR alignment sessions. You landed on three high-impact features for Q3. Then SVP Ramesh walks in with three customer calls and a completely different list.

storybook_pages.title: The Pressure Tactic
storybook_pages.text: Senior stakeholders rarely say 'I disagree with your analysis.' They say 'Every customer I spoke to wants X.' Learning to respond to anecdote with data — without being dismissive — is one of the most valuable skills in any organisation.

storybook_pages.title: Your Turn
storybook_pages.text: Three rounds. You will defend your roadmap. SVP Ramesh will push back with every tool he has — customer stories, urgency, authority. Stay grounded, stay curious, and never just cave.

reflection_prompt: At what point in the debate did you feel most under pressure, and how did you handle it?
